articles.title: Texas wildfire jumps creeks and rivers as powerful winds drive rapid spread
articles.summary: US News: A fast-moving wildfire in north-central Texas has destroyed a family home and business property, burned buildings at a youth camp and forced evacuatio.
articles.body: A fast-moving wildfire in north-central Texas has destroyed a family home and business property, burned buildings at a youth camp and forced evacuations across sparsely populated ranch country west of Fort Worth, while local ranchers opened barns for animals needing evacuation.The Ross Fire began Monday afternoon and spread across more than 78 square miles (200 sq km) in less than 24 hours, moving through lightly populated areas in two counties. Residents said the blaze crossed creeks and rivers as powerful winds pushed it through ranchland.Firefighters had contained only about 8% of the Ross Fire as of Tuesday evening after high temperatures, dry conditions and gusty winds helped drive its rapid spread, according to the news agency Associated Press.Ranchers open barns for livestockRanchers and a livestock commission made barns available to temporarily hold animals needing evacuation. Emergency centres were opened for residents, while some schools cancelled classes.The blaze also threatened ranch properties around Palo Pinto, where aircraft joined crews on the ground in efforts to protect structures."We've thrown everything at this, and we're still having minimal effect," Fire Chief Danny Watkins said.Family business, century-old home destroyedOutside Graford, the fire hit a business that had been in Katie Rochelle's family for generations.The family's canoe rental operation lost its office and repair shop, while a family home built about a century ago was also destroyed. Some of the company's buses and trailers were also destroyed.Rochelle's husband, a local firefighter, helped protect their home overnight as the fire remained active nearby."I don't know how our house survived," Rochelle said. "Now we're waiting and praying."Buildings destroyed at Worth RanchThe fire also reached Worth Ranch, a youth camp on the southern edge of the affected area, destroying several buildings.Scouting America's Longhorn Council said there were no campers or guests at the property when the flames arrived. All personnel were able to leave safely.Officials in Palo Pinto County had confirmed at least five destroyed structures, although authorities were still assessing the extent of the damage.Federal help mobilised as other Texas fires burnTexas Governor Greg Abbott said resources from the Federal Emergency Management Agency would support firefighting efforts. He also urged residents to avoid activities that could start additional fires during the spell of hot, dry and windy weather.The Ross Fire was not the only blaze demanding attention in Texas. Crews were also responding to four smaller wildfires in surrounding Texas counties.More than 50,000 wildfires recorded across USNational Interagency Fire Center data show that more than 50,000 wildfires have been recorded nationwide this year, the highest number for the same point in the year over the past decade. Twelve new large fires were reported on Sunday alone.In Southern California, areas north of Los Angeles were under a red flag warning through Friday, with forecasters warning that new fires could spread rapidly.In Nevada, authorities sharply reduced evacuation orders around Reno after containment of the Hawk Fire reached 85% by Tuesday evening. The blaze had burned about 23 square miles (60 sq km) and destroyed at least 47 homes.Seven people â three first responders and four civilians â were injured. Fire officials said the Hawk Fire was caused by human activity, though investigators had not determined whether it was deliberately set or accidental.Back in Texas, emergency officials expected the Ross Fire to grow further as temperatures rose.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘We Weren’t Super Emotional’ – Jessica Pegula Details How Her Billionaire Parents Influenced Her Personality
articles.summary: Jessica Pegula has an inkling as to where her impressive leadership skills may have come from, tracing them back to one of her parents in particular. Her par...
articles.body:
Jessica Pegula has an inkling as to where her impressive leadership skills may have come from, tracing them back to one of her parents in particular. Her parents, Terry and Kim Pegula, are co-owners of the NFL's Buffalo Bills and the NHL's Buffalo Sabres, with a combined net worth of $9.3 billion, according to Forbes.

What Jessica Pegula Said About Her Parents' Personalities

Pegula arrived at the US Open on the back of runner-up finishes at the Mubadala DC Open and the Cincinnati Open. Riding on that momentum, the American will be aiming to clinch her maiden Grand Slam title at the New York Major when the singles contest gets underway on Sunday, August 30.

Ahead of her campaign, Pegula sat down with Jon Wertheim for a Sports Illustrated interview in which she offered insight into her personality.

After being praised for her leadership skills, the 32-year-old attributed the quality to her directness and communication abilities, traits she believes she inherited from her mother, Kim, who has been incapacitated since suffering a cardiac arrest in 2022.

"Well, that's a nice compliment. I'm very direct, and I think I'm very honest. But I also think I communicate it pretty well, where it's not taken the wrong way. But I'm definitely pretty direct, and I think I don't know if I got that from my mom," Pegula said .

"I want to say I think she was the same way: very direct with what she thought, and I think [she] was pretty thoughtful in the way she always put things, whether it was to employees or to us or stuff around work. So I think I probably got it from my mom," she added.

The world No. 3 revealed that she and her mother had a different temperament from her father Terry's more emotional personality, saying, "We weren't super emotional. I would say my dad's probably a little bit more emotional. I think my mom and I were definitely more the same personality, like kind of laid back."

In contrast to her laid-back demeanor, Pegula shared that her mind typically races during matches and that she often talks to herself on the court.

"I'm very laid back, but at the same time, I'm thinking a lot out on the court, and so I think maybe some people think I just kind of just go with whatever's happening on the court. But I'm actually thinking quite a bit—like a lot. I talk to myself a lot. I'm constantly running," she said.

The world No. 3 disclosed that the same trait carried over when she played other sports recreationally, much to the exasperation of her husband, Taylor Gahagen, during golf sessions.

"I think when I'm competing—even when I play other sports for fun—I love to just talk to myself and talk myself through things a lot of the time out loud," she added. "And that's where, like my husband, if we're playing golf, he's just like, Just hit the ball. I need to talk through things, so maybe it's a little contradictory with my laid-backness."

MORE: Jessica Pegula, Coco Gauff Applaud Emma Navarro's Billionaire Parents at Cincinnati Open – 'You've Been Great to Me'

Jessica Pegula has already begun her US Open campaign, competing in the mixed doubles event alongside fellow American Taylor Fritz. The duo failed to make a deep run in the contest, as Diana Shnaider and Casper Ruud claimed a 4-2, 4-1 victory in their first-round clash.

articles.title: LeBron James’ LLC borrowed $300 million from Mark Walter-led Guggenheim before joining LA Lakers
articles.summary: Prior to either of their associations with the LA Lakers, Mark Walter’s Guggenheim Partners lent LeBron James $300 million for a new company. In 2018, as Jam...
articles.body:
Prior to either of their associations with the LA Lakers , Mark Walter's Guggenheim Partners lent LeBron James $300 million for a new company.

In 2018, as James geared up to sign with the Lakers in free agency, part of his decision to move to the City of Angels was because of his desire to pursue outside business ventures.

Part of this involved setting up a new LLC, which required a massive injection of cash flow. Unbeknownst to him at the time, the man who would end up buying the Lakers seven years later played a crucial part in this.

LeBron James' LLC borrowed $300 million from Mark Walter's Guggenheim Partners

According to reporting from Bloomberg , just a few months prior to him signing with the Los Angeles Lakers, LeBron James got into business with future team owner Mark Walter.

In 2018, James' LLC borrowed $300 million from two life insurance companies that were associated with Guggenheim Partners.

At the time, Walter was the CEO of Guggenheim Partners. The amount is due in 2049, allowing James the cash flow his company needed, being leveraged against James' sponsorship and non-NBA earnings.

Furthermore, in 2022, James signed a $97 million contract extension with the Lakers. At the same time, his LLC borrowed more cash from the pair of insurance companies against bonds worth $60 million with an interest rate of 5.75%.

These transactions were approved by the NBA at the time, as they explained in a statement to Fox Business when asked about the matter.

"The 2018 and 2022 transactions were a securitisation done by Mr. James with his personal, non-NBA salary, assets and income, which is a very common financial structure for an individual with this level of earnings and assets.

"Both transactions were fully approved by NBA. Mr. James has no affiliation with Guggenheim, Sammons Financial, North American Life or Midland National beyond their participation in these transactions."

Fast forward to the summer of 2025, and James would become a direct associate of Walter, who purchased the LA Lakers for a then-record $10 billion.

Since James' departure this summer, Walter has sold the Lakers to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner for a whopping $12.5 billion, amid an investigation into his financial activity.

articles.title: Ziolkowski in talks to join Monza on loan, Parma’s offer for permanent transfer denied
articles.summary: Jan Ziolkowski could leave Roma in the final days of the transfer window. Following the arrival of Koulierakis, the Polish defender, awaiting approval today...
articles.body:
Jan Ziolkowski could leave Roma in the final days of the transfer window.

Following the arrival of Koulierakis , the Polish defender, awaiting approval today for the transfer of Oosterwolde , who can also play in a back three, has fallen to the back row and risks limited playing time this season.

The 2005-born defender is popular with some foreign clubs, but in the last few hours, Monza has moved into pole position, even overtaking Parma .

Roma had inquired about signing Ziolkowski for around €7-8 million, in addition to two foreign clubs who had made official offers to Roma. However, at this price, Roma are now prioritizing a loan move.

In the last few hours, Monza has outbid Parma and two foreign clubs to sign Ziolkowski.

As Fabrizio Romano reports, the Giallorossi are giving priority to the Brianza club, partly because of the terms offered: a loan deal that could allow the 2005-born player to develop and become a valuable asset within a season.

Otherwise, he would be sold in 2027. It is understood that a potential permanent offer outside of the market could reshuffle the cards and change the situation. Further discussions between Roma and Monza are expected today.

articles.title: How will Barcelona line up against Athletic?
articles.summary: Hansi Flick’s possible XI for Thursday’s clash
articles.body:
Barcelona look for a strong start to their La Liga home campaign as the reigning back-to-back champions face historic rivals Athletic Club at Camp Nou.

Here's how we think Hansi Flick will line up his troops for Thursday's battle:

Barça got off to an excellent start at the weekend against Elche and now return home where they finished last season with a historic perfect record at Camp Nou, and Flick will be looking to ride the momentum of the team that played so well in the second half on Sunday.

We will likely see only one change at the back since Andreas Christensen needs to be managed carefully and isn't expected to start two games in four days, so Pau Cubarsí will probably make his season debut after his summer glory with Spain.

Gerard Martín is Cubarsí's trusted partner and will start again at center-back, with Eric Garcia picked ahead of Jules Kounde at right-back and young Xavi Espart retaining his place on the left given the fact João Cancelo is still not fully fit and Alejandro Balde 's status is uncertain at best.

Even though Gavi survived an injury scare at the weekend and only suffered a bruise on his knee, it's prudent not to risk him in this one so Pedri will take his place in the lineup alongside Marc Bernal and Fermín López .

We are all excited to see the debut of new signing Rodri that could very well happen in this one, but he's had just a couple of sessions with the squad and will likely come off the bench to get a great ovation from the home crowd in the second half.

Barça's attack put on a show in the second half on Sunday and the noise about the striker position has quieted down for now, especially after Raphinha 's amazing performance as a center-forward. He will start in that spot again, with Karim Adeyemi keeping his place on the left after an excellent competitive debut at the weekend.

Lamine Yamal is very much in preseason form and needs minutes to gain rhythm, so the teenager will start again on the right looking to bounce back from a supbar display against Elche.

Possible XI : Joan; Eric, Cubarsí, Martín, Espart; Fermín, Bernal, Pedri; Yamal, Raphinha, Adeyemi (4-3-3)

articles.title: Report: Ipswich Town set to land €27.5m World Cup winner
articles.summary: Exequiel Palacios to Ipswich? Why This Argentina Midfielder Link Feels SignificantIpswich Town’s summer rebuild in midfield already has a clear shape, and th...
articles.body:
Exequiel Palacios to Ipswich? Why This Argentina Midfielder Link Feels Significant

Ipswich Town's summer rebuild in midfield already has a clear shape, and the latest report adds another intriguing layer. According to The Athletic , Ipswich have already moved decisively, with "Ipswich have signed midfielders Sasa Lukic from Fulham and Florentino Luis from Burnley this summer, after Jens Cajuste and Dan Neil departed the club following the conclusion of their loan spells."

That alone tells the story of a club refusing to stand still. Ipswich are refreshing the engine room with experience, physicality and pedigree, and Exequiel Palacios would elevate that strategy again. The 27-year-old arrives in this conversation with serious credentials. As outlined in the report, "Palacios, 27, joined Leverkusen from River Plate in 2020." In that time, "He has made 185 appearances for the club, providing 15 goals and 17 assists, and was part of the side that won the Bundesliga title in 2023-24."

For Ipswich, that sort of background matters. This is not a developmental gamble in the usual sense, it is a player who has operated in title-winning environments and handled the demands of top-level football in Germany and on the international stage. There is, of course, context around his recent availability. "He featured 25 times in all competitions last season either side of four months out with a right adductor injury." That will naturally be part of any assessment, especially for a side looking to add reliability as well as quality.

Still, the ceiling is obvious. "Palacios has been capped 41 times at international level by Argentina." More than that, "He was part of the side that won the 2022 World Cup and was included in the squad for the 2026 tournament but featured just once in the tournament in their final group game against Jordan ." Even limited recent tournament minutes do not diminish the stature he would bring to Portman Road.

From an Ipswich perspective, this would signal intent. Lukic and Florentino Luis suggest structure and control, while Palacios would add craft, composure and proven quality in possession. For a club trying to establish itself and push forward under Gary O'Neil, signing a midfielder with Bundesliga and Argentina pedigree would represent a notable statement.

The attraction here is not only reputation, it is fit. Ipswich needed to respond after losing Cajuste and Neil, and they appear to be targeting players who can immediately raise the standard. If this move progresses, it could become one of the most eye-catching deals of their summer.

As an Ipswich supporter, this is exactly the kind of report that gets you excited. We all knew the midfield needed fresh energy after the loan departures, but bringing in players with this calibre would feel like a major step forward. Lukic and Florentino Luis already suggest the club are thinking bigger, smarter and with real purpose. If Palacios joins that mix, suddenly this midfield has depth, authority and proper top-level know-how.

What stands out most is the mentality he would bring. Anyone who has been around a Bundesliga title-winning squad and an Argentina set-up packed with elite players understands pressure, expectation and quality. That can rub off on everyone around him. At a club like Ipswich, where momentum and belief mean so much, that matters enormously.

There will be some concern over the injury record, and that is fair. Missing four months is not a minor issue. But this is where trust in the recruitment team comes in. If Ipswich believe he is ready and the medical side checks out, then it is easy to see why supporters would back the move.

Most of all, this report feels like confirmation that Ipswich are not here to make up the numbers. These are not timid moves. These are ambitious midfield targets, and fans should embrace that. If the club can land someone of Palacios' profile, Portman Road will believe anything is possible this season.

articles.title: Bayern Munich cult hero Luca Toni believes Harry Kane should win the Ballon d’Or
articles.summary: Game recognises game. Luca Toni joins the Harry Kane Ballon d’Or train… and so should you. He’s the world’s best.
articles.body:
Yes, that's how we start this segment. An icon in every sense of the word.

With 322 career goals, the Italian football legend and former Bayern Munich star is the fourth most prolific scorer his nation has ever produced. He's won pretty much every individual award as a striker and had a massive role in Italy 's 2006 World Cup win. So yes, the striker role is his bread and butter.

Luca was at the presentation ceremony for the European Golden Boot 2025/26. A trophy won by none other than another Bayern Munich striker… (Sir?) Harry Edward Kane.

During the presentation ceremony, Luca had a couple of iconic things to say (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), with him first requesting Kane to "please stop breaking all our records". For context, no player outside of Lionel Messi has EVER scored more goals in a single season. 73 goals for club and country, with a whopping 61 (!!!) goals for Bayern Munich last season.

Bayern fans certainly want this to continue.

Most importantly, Luca is aboard the Kane Ballon d'Or 2026 hype train. "You deserve to win the Ballon d'Or," concluded the former striker.

Heck, a mic drop would've been perfect. But yes, there you have it. Yet another icon voicing his support for Kane's Ballon d'Or bid. Sure, the award has been a scam for a while now, but surely 81 goal contributions in a single season gets the job done? SURELY???!!!

articles.title: Red Bull Gets Second Chance at Power Unit Upgrade
articles.summary: Red Bull has the fate of its engine hanging in the balance, at least when it comes to making improvements this season.
articles.body:
Red Bull has the fate of its engine hanging in the balance, at least when it comes to making improvements this season.

During the last Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) check at the start of the season, Red Bull was found to have the strongest power unit.

There was a full-on bench test, where Red Bull was deemed more than 2% ahead of every other manufacturer, meaning no extra development time, spending, or ability to introduce a new power unit upgrade.

ZANDVOORT, NETHERLANDS – AUGUST 22: Max Verstappen of the Netherlands driving the (3) Oracle Red Bull Racing RB22 Red Bull Ford Powertrains on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Netherlands at Circuit Zandvoort on August 22, 2026 in Zandvoort, Netherlands. (Photo by Simon Galloway/LAT Images) // Getty Images

Red Bull fought the assessment directly with the FIA, but in the end, FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis and the regulatory body found it a valid conclusion.

"Our measurement, in my opinion, has proven to be very accurate," he said.

"With that said, has everything worked fine? No, because obviously people are not happy and so on. So do we need to think about improvements in the future? Yes, I would say so."

Now, before the Italian Grand Prix, there will be a second ADUO review that could give Red Bull a second chance to get extra development support.

At this point, Red Bull is at best the third-fastest car at most tracks, but usually the fourth- or third-fastest.

An engine upgrade could be what takes their car into race-winning contention.

Max Verstappen | Photo Credit: Red Bull Content Pool

However, Tombazis is not convinced these upgrades are worthwhile or impactful in the grand scheme of things.

"I don't think it would be convenient for you to always be below, just to sort of keep getting more opportunities," he said. "What's the point of opportunities if it isn't ultimately for you to be on top?

"I think the system is working as it was designed. I do think there are some weaknesses that we need to address in the future, for sure, to make it less time-consuming, less controversial. We do need to make some steps to improve it in the future."

Red Bull, while doing a ton of aerodynamic work, begs to differ and will fight for a power unit development opportunity and a chance to challenge the class-leading Mercedes car.

articles.title: Major gangland figure Steven Daniel arrested in organised crime raid
articles.summary: Steven 'Bonzo' Daniel was arrested on Wednesday at his home in the north of Glasgow.
articles.body:
One of Scotland's most high-profile gangland figures has been arrested during an early morning police raid.

Steven 'Bonzo' Daniel, 46 was taken into custody at around 06:00 from his home in Robroyston in the north of Glasgow.

Daniel is understood to be the head of the notorious Daniel crime family which has been engaged in a violent feud with the rival Lyons family for 25 years.

He was arrested in connection with serious and organised crime, firearms and drugs offences as part of Operation Ventetic, a major UK-wide operation which has dismantled several gangs.

BBC Scotland News joined the operation shortly before sunrise.

Dozens of officers involved were briefed at a nearby police station before joining a convoy to Daniel's home.

Two uniformed officers initially approached the property and spoke to him through a first-floor window.

An officer with a police dog then moved in.

Moments later Daniel left the property through the front door and was taken into the back of a police van.

A second man, Steven Gordon, 39 was also arrested in Garthamlock, less than four miles away, in a simultaneous operation.

He was taken into custody in connection with serious and organised crime, firearms and drugs offences and conspiracy to murder.

Assistant Chief Constable Dave Ferry said: "The chief constable has made it clear that those intent on being involved in serious and organised crime will be brought to justice.

"This enforcement action underlines that commitment.

"We will continue to take strong action and to use every tool and tactic available to relentlessly pursue those involved in serious criminality who seek to profit from the harm and misery they cause to communities in Scotland."

The Scottish arm of Operation Venetic has resulted in more than 60 arrests since 2020 when the National Crime Agency penetrated a secret communications system used by criminals.

In May 2017 Daniel suffered serious facial wounds when he was attacked after a 100mph car chase through Glasgow.

articles.title: 4 things to watch for Commanders in joint practice with Ravens

The Washington Commanders headed to Owings Mills, Md., on Tuesday for Wednesday's scheduled joint practice with the Baltimore Ravens . After Saturday's disappointing performance in a 17-13 loss to the Detroit Lions , Wednesday's practice holds more weight than the final preseason game on Friday.

While the final preseason game could determine a few final roster spots for the Commanders, the joint practice with Baltimore is a final opportunity for Washington's starters to get some work against the Ravens' starters. It matters for the Commanders because their starting offense didn't play in the first preseason game and had only three snaps in the loss at Detroit.

What does Washington need to see in Wednesday's practice? Here are four things to watch on Wednesday in Owings Mills.

By all accounts, Daniels has enjoyed an excellent training camp. He looks comfortable in David Blough 's new offense. His accuracy has matched what we saw in his 2024 rookie season. So far, so good, but the Commanders would like to see Daniels have a successful day against the Ravens. Remember, he performed well against the Dolphins in the joint practice two weeks ago, but Baltimore presents a very different challenge. With Daniels unlikely to play in Friday's preseason finale, Wednesday's practice is his final regular-season tuneup. A strong performance against the Ravens from Daniels and the first-team offense would alleviate some of the concerns that arose from Saturday's performance.

This story continues to evolve. It feels like we've been discussing this position since March. Washington still doesn't know what it has in Nick Allegretti at center because he lacks experience there. But the Commanders have repeatedly expressed confidence in the veteran. He will not participate, as he continues to recover from a calf strain that has sidelined him all camp. Washington knows what it has in Julian Good-Jones. He's not a starting-quality player. The Commanders should give rookie Matt Gulbin the entire scrimmage to work with each quarterback, especially Daniels. He needs the reps. It will be interesting to see how Gulbin performs against Baltimore's front seven. This is a big test.

With Washington's starters on the practice field on Wednesday, which receiver will line up as the No. 3 receiver behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs ? While Blough isn't going to show too much in a practice or preseason game, we'll learn a lot by seeing who gets most of the reps as the third wideout. Luke McCaffrey , Treylon Burks , Antonio Williams , Dyami Brown , Van Jefferson and Jaden Bradley will all get some run, but this could be a test to see who the Commanders trust the most as WR3.

With Will Harris gone, Washington's safety position is set. We know the five the Commanders will keep and have a good idea of their roles. At cornerback, things are less certain. We know Mike Sainristil and Amik Robertson are the top two, with Trey Amos still out. Baltimore's receivers, specifically Zay Flowers , will present a unique challenge for the secondary. How will the Commanders handle Flowers' quickness and his release? Who will have the responsibility of covering Flowers? The corner position remains a concern heading into the regular season with Ahkello Witherspoon 's retirement and Amos' injury. It wouldn't be shocking to see Washington add another cornerback, but this group has another chance to impress against the Ravens.

articles.title: South Korea police find four bodies on Jeju island as missing persons scandal deepens
articles.summary: A police sergeant has been arrested following accusations that he lied to victims' families and prematurely closed missing persons cases.
articles.body:
Four missing people have been found dead on South Korean holiday island Jeju, as local police face mounting public criticism for allegedly mishandling missing persons cases.

Reports emerged last week that authorities were launching a belated search for a woman reported missing months ago. This sparked criticism of the police for failing to search for her earlier.

The scandal has since deepened with the arrest of a police sergeant, surnamed Bu, who is accused of lying to victims' families and prematurely closing missing persons cases.

Four officers in the sergeant's chain of command have been put on administrative leave and on Tuesday President Lee Jae Myung ordered a sweeping reform of the police force.

Since Saturday, police have found four bodies on the island, including that of 37-year-old Jang Mi-ran who had gone missing in May.

On Monday, her body was located at a palm tree farm about 500 metres (547 yards) from where she was staying. She was believed to have killed herself.

Bu is suspected to have closed Jang's case prematurely without confirming her whereabouts.

According to local reports, Bu had allegedly told Jang's boyfriend that he had spoken to Jang over the phone and she had told Bu she did not wish to speak to her boyfriend.

Police also found the body of a man in his 60s from Jeju City on Saturday.

The man had gone missing on 28 June. Bu had closed his case and reportedly told the family that the man was found "safe" but "does not wish to disclose his location to the family".

"We believed the police when they said my father was safe and waited, but after 51 days, what returned was his body," the man's son told reporters.

It is not yet clear whether Bu was involved in the missing persons cases for two other bodies that were found in coastal villages in recent days.

Police are now examining all the missing persons reports that Bu had handled, which number nearly 300.

Jeju is one of South Korea's most popular tourist destinations.

The island, known for its rows of palm trees and sparkling waters, received more than 13 million foreign and domestic visitors last year.

While violent crime is rare in South Korea, suicide rates are among the highest in the world.

Some experts have said the low crime rate is part of the reason why missing persons cases are not taken seriously.

"After experiencing on the field that the absolute majority of missing adults are found quickly, [the officers] tend to assume all cases are like that," Lee Yung-hyeock, a professor specialising in police science at Konkuk University, told Yonhap news agency.

While more than 70,000 adults are reported missing in South Korea each year, 99% of them are marked as resolved within a month.

On Tuesday, President Lee said during a Cabinet meeting that "the recent breakdown in police discipline and irresponsibility in public safety matters have become serious problems".

Pointing out that the police are likely to wield the most power out of all the state's institutions, he said "the Korean people are questioning whether [the police] deserve this large power".

South Korea's national police chief was grilled by lawmakers at an emergency National Assembly hearing on Monday, during which he admitted that "there is a fault in the system".

This scandal comes at a politically sensitive time for South Korea's police.

The government had recently passed reform to transfer full investigative power from the prosecutors to the police, a move they said was intended to curtail the prosecutors' influence in politics.

However, the reform has been unpopular among the public, who have for many years accused the police of corruption and incompetence.

With reporting by Hosu Lee and Leehyun Choi in Seoul

articles.title: Islamabad: At least 14 babies die in Pakistan hospital fire
articles.summary: The fire broke out in an air conditioning unit at the mother and child unit in one of Islamabad's main hospitals.
articles.body:
At least 14 newborn babies have died in a fire on a hospital ward in Pakistan's capital Islamabad.

The fire broke out on the third floor of the mother and child unit of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) hospital, one of the main state-run hospitals in the city, on Wednesday morning.

An air conditioning unit caught fire, a spokesman for the hospital told the BBC.

There were 15 babies in the ward when the fire broke out, a hospital spokesman said. One baby was rescued.

The babies in the ward were either in incubators or hooked on oxygen equipment, Pakistan's Health Minister Mustafa Kamal told Geo News. Oxygen is not flammable on its own, but it can accelerate a fire, making materials burn hotter and faster.

Emergency responders rescued at least 19 other people from the hospital, including 10 women, seven children and two men.

The newborn babies who died in the fire have been badly burnt, and will need to be identified in through DNA tests, police said.

Only after the DNA tests can the bodies be returned to their parents.

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed his "deep sorrow and heartfelt regret" over the hospital fire, and instructed the authorities to "conduct an immediate investigation", according to the statement from his office.

"Such a situation with children is irreparable", the statement said.

Islamabad's District Magistrate has formed a fact-finding committee to investigate the fire which must produce a report "within 24 hours".

Outside the hospital, one man told the BBC his three-day-old baby had died in the fire.

There was a sense of shock among the families who gathered by the entrance, crying by the side of the ward.

Hivsa Walid told the BBC she was inside the hospital when the fire broke out, with her sister-in-law who had given birth in the days before.

She said they were in the nursery opposite the room where the fire started. They heard a shout and initially thought someone had died but then saw the smoke. They grabbed the baby - who is so young she's not yet been named - and ran.

Police have been patrolling the entrance of the hospital, and the glass from shattered windows lay scattered on the pavement mixed with medical masks.

The PIMS is one of the biggest hospitals in Pakistan's capital, with 156 beds in its maternal and child health unit.

Pakistan has dealt with a number of major fires in recent years, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement.

In January, a fire ripped through the Gul Plaza shopping centre in Pakistan's largest city of Karachi, killing 67 people.

articles.summary: Tech News News: Instagram head Adam Mosseri has said that only a small percentage of teenagers used Instagram's âTake a Breakâ feature before the company made it a de.
articles.body: Instagram head Adam Mosseri has said that only a small percentage of teenagers used Instagram's âTake a Breakâ feature before the company made it a default setting for young users. The feature, which encourages users to step away from Instagram after spending a set amount of time on the app, became a key point of discussion during an ongoing US trial examining whether Meta designed Instagram and Facebook in ways that could make children addicted to them. âMost teens didn't want it,â Mosseri said. âWe decided to push forward with it anyway.âAdam Mosseri said the feature was used by only a low-single-digit percentage of teenagers before Instagram changed its approach in September 2024, nearly three years after launching it.Instagram's 'Take a Break' feature and teen safety under scrutinyAdam Mosseri, who has led Instagram since 2018, testified in a federal court in Oakland, California, as part of a lawsuit brought by 29 US states against Meta. When an attorney representing Colorado questioned him, Mosseri acknowledged that few teenagers had used the âTake a Breakâ feature before it was turned on by default. However, he rejected claims that Instagram deliberately delayed making the safety feature the default option.When the feature was launched in December 2021, Mosseri had said that early tests showed more than 90% of teenagers who turned it on continued using it. The feature encourages users to close Instagram and take a break after a set period.The case is being closely watched as one of the biggest legal tests of social media's impact on young users.US states accuse Meta of designing addictive platformsFour states â California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey â have accused Meta of designing its platforms in ways that could keep young users engaged and contribute to anxiety, depression and suicide. Meta has denied the allegations and said its research found no clear link between adolescents' social media use and a lack of well-being.All 29 states involved in the lawsuit have also accused Meta of improperly collecting and using the personal data of children under 13. The states could seek nearly $200 billion in civil penalties, according to Reuters.Mosseri also denied allegations that Instagram tried to hide information related to children's safety. âI am not trying to encourage my team to hide anything,â he said. âI want to understand how things work. articles.title: Meet Nimaya Williams, the North Carolina junior who completed free college-planning steps and became one of only two students nationwide to receive a $40,000 BigFuture scholarship
articles.summary: US News: For many high-school students, preparing for life after graduation can feel overwhelming. College applications, career choices, financial planning, an.
articles.body: For many high-school students, preparing for life after graduation can feel overwhelming. College applications, career choices, financial planning, and scholarship searches can all seem like separate challenges, especially for students who are still figuring out what they want their future to look like. For Nimaya Williams, a junior at Westover High School in Fayetteville, North Carolina, taking practical steps toward that future recently brought an unexpected reward: a $40,000 scholarship that could help change the course of her college journey. Williams was selected by College Board's BigFuture as one of only two students nationwide to receive the monthly $40,000 BigFuture Scholarship, according to a July 2026 news release from Cumberland County Schools. She earned the award by completing college and career planning activities through BigFuture, College Board's free online platform.A surprise worth $40,000Williams did not expect her college-planning efforts to result in such a major award. When she received the surprise announcement, the Westover High School junior was overcome with emotion. âIâm about to cry. This is life changing,â Williams said in the Cumberland County Schools release, adding that she felt she was âdestined to do great things.âThe recognition came as Williams worked through the steps offered by BigFuture, a platform designed to help students prepare for life after high school. Rather than requiring students to win an academic competition or submit a traditional scholarship essay, the programme rewards eligible students for taking proactive steps toward college and career planning. For Williams, those actions ultimately led to one of the programme's largest monthly awards.Turning planning into opportunityThe BigFuture Scholarship is connected to activities that encourage students to think seriously about their futures. BigFuture helps students explore potential careers, prepare for college, and find ways to finance higher education. Williams' story highlights that college preparation does not necessarily begin with filling out an application. It can start much earlier, with students exploring career interests, learning about colleges, and thinking about how they will finance their education.That approach can be particularly important for high-school students who may not yet have a detailed plan for what comes after graduation. Taking smaller steps can help make a complicated process more manageable. Williams' scholarship also demonstrates how planning can sometimes open unexpected doors for students.A major relief for her familyThe $40,000 award could have an impact beyond Williams herself. Her mother, Shantay Dupree, said the scholarship would create more opportunities for her daughter while easing some of the financial pressure surrounding college. Dupree said Williams has many strengths and described the scholarship as an important step toward her future. She also acknowledged that paying for college can be difficult for families when money is tight.For families facing the rising cost of higher education, a scholarship of this size can make a meaningful difference. It can reduce the amount the student and family need to cover through savings, loans, or other financial assistance. The award therefore represents more than a moment of recognition for Williams. Since the programme began in 2019, BigFuture has awarded more than $25 million in scholarships to more than 30,000 students who took proactive steps toward their futures, according to the school district's announcement. That makes Williams' achievement part of a broader effort to encourage students to begin preparing for college and careers before graduation.A step toward her futureWilliams' story shows that preparing for college does not always have to mean accomplishing something extraordinary overnight. Sometimes, it begins with completing one planning activity, exploring a career, or learning more about financing education. Her decision to take those steps through BigFuture ultimately brought an unexpected $40,000 opportunity.For Williams and her family, the scholarship arrives at an important point in her high-school journey. With another year before graduation, she now has additional financial support as she considers what comes next. articles.title: Kriti Sanon Rakhi ad: Giva jewellery drops Bollywood actor's Indian festival ad over outfit
articles.summary: Kriti Sanon has defended the ad in which she was seen celebrating the upcoming Hindu festival of Rakhi.
articles.body:
An Indian jewellery brand has removed their new advertisement for the upcoming festival of Rakshabandhan, also known as Rakhi, after backlash over the outfit worn by the female lead.

The ad featured popular Bollywood actor Kriti Sanon celebrating the Hindu festival in which sisters tie a thread called Rakhi over their brothers' wrists.

Sanon, who is seen in a cropped top, skirt and a cape, addressed her critics on Tuesday night saying "culture and traditions are in a woman's heart, not in her neckline!"

The row started earlier on Tuesday after actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut called the ad "intentionally creepy" and asked why someone would tie a Rakhi dressed in a bikini.

In her comments posted on social media, Ranaut did not name Sanon, but appeared to be referring to the actor.

"It is a wonderful time to be a woman, our closets are full of variety of clothes... From all the options that are available to us today why would you tie your brother a Rakhi in your bikini/under garments? Where are all your styling options? The advert looks intentionally creepy," she wrote.

Her remarks quickly drew attention online, with some users echoing her criticism of Sanon's outfit saying it was too revealing and inappropriate for a traditional festival.

One commentator described her top as a bralette, saying there was a "clear line between modern styling and basic sensitivity towards Hindu festivals".

"Pairing a bralette outfit with a sacred occasion like Rakshabandhan felt completely out of touch and unnecessary," she posted on X.

Others objected to a scene in the advertisement in which the actor also ties a rakhi on her pet dog.

But Sanon also received support, including from Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, who defended her, saying what a woman chose to wear was her own decision. Others accused Ranaut of moral policing.

Some also pointed out that though Ranaut has been more conservative in her clothing in recent years after becoming a politician, she herself often wore short dresses and Western outfits in her films and at social gatherings.

Sanon responded to the critics in an Instagram story, calling out the mindset that questioned women for their sartorial choices. Like Ranaut, she did not name anyone directly.

"The essence of festivals is not in the clothes you wear, it is in the emotions and meaning you hold for the traditions... When will we stop telling women what to wear?? Ethnic fashion has evolved over the years, but still a woman's respect for her culture is measured with just her clothes!! Culture & Traditions are in her heart, not in her neckline!"

Sanon also addressed the issue of tying Rakhi to her pet, saying though the festival traditionally celebrates the bond between a brother and sister, its spirit was about protecting loved ones - which, for her, included her sister and her pet.

Despite her spirited defence, jewellery company Giva announced on Wednesday it was pulling the ad.

"We have the highest regard and deep respect for Indian culture, traditions and festivals. As a brand, we have always believed in celebrating these joyous moments with the entire family and this time we wanted to extend the love and celebration to our pets," Giva said in a statement , external on Instagram.

Why India is talking about ripped jeans and knees

The Indian woman who stood up to moral policing - and won a pageant

"If our recent advertisement has inadvertently hurt the sentiments of some segments of society, that was not our intent at all. Out of respect, we have withdrawn the advertisement from all media," it added.

Giva is not the first Indian brand to withdraw an ad after criticism on social media. In 2020, popular jewellery brand Tanishq withdrew an advertisement featuring an interfaith couple after it faced right-wing backlash online.

Debates over what women should - and shouldn't - wear have also repeatedly sparked controversy in India.

Last year, a beauty pageant contestant was commended for standing up to a group of men who tried to bully her and other contestants over the skirts and western dresses they were wearing.

In 2021, there was outrage after a 19-year-old student, who turned up in shorts to take an exam, was forced to wrap a curtain around her legs after the teacher objected to her clothes.

In the same year, thousands of women - and some men - shared photos of themselves wearing ripped jeans after the chief minister of the northern state of Uttarakhand criticised a woman for wearing them.

articles.title: The RSF’s defeat will not end Sudan’s war but merely fragment it
articles.summary: Sudanese army’s battlefield gains rely on an armed coalition it may struggle to control once the common enemy is gone.
articles.body:
Sudan’s army has had a good summer. Last month, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) recaptured several towns along the strategic Export Road, known locally as Sadirat, which connects the central Nile valley to the country’s west, and pushed the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) into a defensive crouch across much of the centre of the country.

On the back of these gains, SAF leaders are now speaking more confidently of defeating the RSF entirely, rather than merely containing it.

But look east, to Sudan’s Blue Nile state, and the picture inverts. In mid-August, the RSF and its ally, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (led by Abdulaziz al-Hilu), retook Kurmuk and seized Geisan within days, in attacks that Sudanese military sources said were launched from across the border in Ethiopia. Drone attacks on multiple army-controlled cities this month also showed that the RSF’s reach extends well beyond Darfur, its main territorial stronghold.

The lesson of the summer, then, is not that the SAF is on the verge of decisive victory. It is that military victory and political resolution are becoming two very different things. Even a full RSF defeat may not end Sudan’s war so much as fracture it into several smaller conflicts.

A look at the coalitions doing the fighting helps explain why. The anti-RSF coalition is coordinated and led by the SAF, but the army also relies on allied armed movements, including Darfuri factions that signed the 2020 Juba Peace Agreement (JPA). These include Finance Minister Gibril Ibrahim’s Justice and Equality Movement (JEM) and the Sudan Liberation Movement, led by Darfur Governor Minni Minnawi. The JPA required their forces to be integrated into Sudan’s military and security services, but they have been reluctant to give up the military autonomy that underpins their political leverage.

Yasser al-Atta, then assistant commander-in-chief and now army chief of staff, announced in March that the army would activate mechanisms to organise and integrate allied irregular groups into the formal military and security services, but little has happened since.

Al-Atta wasn’t even the first to promise to address the problems of the proliferation of weapons and armed groups. Two years earlier, deputy commander-in-chief Shams al-Din Kabbashi told a graduation ceremony for Minni Minnawi’s Sudan Liberation Movement fighters that the army had “begun enacting a law and structures to control the many popular resistance groups”, warning that the array of semi-autonomous militias, tribal coalitions and volunteers backing the SAF’s war efforts, the “popular resistance” as it is called, would “become the next danger if we continue this way”.

More than two years on from Kabbashi’s speech, the underlying problem remains largely unresolved.

Then there is the RSF’s own coalition, which is actively fragmenting. A string of senior figures, al-Nour al-Qubba, al-Savanna, and more recently, the RSF-appointed governor for the Kordofan region, Hamad Khalifa, have defected, amid reports of Saudi financial inducements as well as tribal grievances.

When al-Nour al-Qubba left, he took dozens of combat vehicles and a large contingent of fighters with him. Given that the RSF is a franchise more than a unified fighting force, these defections should worry the SAF as much as they comfort it: defectors often arrive as intact forces loyal to their commanders, not soldiers used to reporting to a chain of command. In a way, the SAF inherits the RSF’s structural weakness with each defection.

Another example is Abu Aqla Keikel, an SAF-trained officer who initially fought on the army’s side after the war erupted in 2023, before defecting to the RSF later that year and then back to the SAF in October 2024. His Sudan Shield Forces remain, in practice, more under his own command than the army’s, even as he appears alongside SAF leadership and Darfuri commanders at recent battlefield-victory photo ops.

Many commanders inside the anti-RSF camp maintain a fairly wide margin of operational independence and consequently their own political calculations. This will become far more apparent once the war ends and there is no longer a common enemy to paper over the differences.

Sudan’s Islamists, meanwhile, occupy a strange position. Brigades like al-Baraa ibn Malik, affiliated with Sudan’s Islamic Movement, which underpinned Omar al-Bashir’s former ruling National Congress Party (NCP), supplied thousands of fighters and were instrumental in retaking Khartoum from the RSF. The United States has sanctioned al-Baraa ibn Malik, while the European Union has sanctioned its leader, al-Misbah Abu Zaid. Amid this international pressure and SAF battlefield gains, some Islamist fighters and leaders have begun pulling back, in what one Sudan Tribune report described as a “tactical withdrawal”. Al-Misbah recently posted that “we have returned to our civilian lives”.

But retreating from the battlefield is not the same as retreating from politics. Ahmed Haroun, chairman of the former ruling NCP, told Reuters news agency last year that the Islamic Movement could support an extended period of army rule, with an eye towards returning to government through “the ballot box”, as Haroun put it.

Indeed, another potential flashpoint for the SAF is that the war has given fighters in Islamist brigades like al-Baraa ibn Malik years of battlefield experience. There is little reason to think fighters who helped recapture the capital will disarm and disband the moment the war is over, at least not without a political settlement that creates a path for demobilisation.

This is the context in which SAF chief and de facto president General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan’s recently announced national dialogue should be read, less as a comprehensive resolution to the country’s militia problem than as a political process that could convert the army’s wartime alliances into post-war influence.

Burhan has explicitly ruled out the return of RSF leaders to power, promising there would be no “ incomplete peace ” that allowed Hemedti or other RSF leaders back into government. Given the RSF’s abysmal human rights record during the war, the exclusion is defensible, but the broader armed-group problem remains unresolved: namely, how the RSF’s remaining forces would actually be dismantled or integrated, particularly in Darfur, and how the SAF’s own allied militias would be brought under a single chain of command once the shooting slows down.

Another structural problem that is older than this war reinforces why claims of total victory remain elusive. The Sudanese army has long struggled to project sustained power across the country’s peripheries. Under Omar al-Bashir, the government relied on Janjaweed militias to help the army fight the rebellion in Darfur. In 2013, many Janjaweed fighters were brought into the newly created RSF.

There is little reason to think a hollowed-out, cash-poor SAF, dependent on volunteer recruits, Islamist militias and Juba Peace Agreement signatory forces, can now succeed where the pre-war state repeatedly struggled: in Darfur, a region roughly the size of France, where the RSF continues to use cross-border supply routes.

Even if the RSF is somehow eventually broken, its weapons and its fighters will not simply disappear. They will pass to whichever political entrepreneur is best positioned to pick them up. Meanwhile, in Khartoum, the questions of the day after will pry open conflicts that the war has, for now, kept closed.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

articles.title: In the 1940s, a New York handyman began expanding a cabin with railroad ties and cast-off objects; it grew into a seven-storey labyrinth with around 35 caverns and alcoves
articles.summary: US News: Explore the extraordinary story of Clarence Schmidt's House of Mirrors, a unique seven-storey architectural marvel built from discarded materials in Woodstock, NY. Learn about its origins, growth, and artistic significance.
articles.body: Clarence Schmidt did not set out to build one of Americaâs strangest houses. What began as a modest cabin on a wooded mountainside in Woodstock, New York, became an enormous handmade environment of rooms, walkways, balconies, gardens, grottoes and shrines. Built without a conventional architectural plan, the structure expanded as Schmidt found new materials, developed new ideas and reshaped the landscape around him. At its fullest form, the House of Mirrors extended nearly seven storeys down the mountainside and contained roughly 35 caverns and alcoves.According to Philadelphiaâs Magic Gardens, Clarence Schmidt (1897â1978) moved to Woodstock in the 1940s and, having trained as a mason and plasterer, found work as a handyman. His first home, Journeyâs End, began as a simple log cabin made from railroad ties. Schmidt tarred the exterior and covered it with cracked glass, transforming the modest cabin into an unusual reflective structure. The cabin became the starting point for a much larger environment, which Schmidt expanded and altered as he developed the mountainside site.A cabin that kept growingBy the 1940s, Schmidt was reshaping the mountainside around his home. He cleared sections of the steep slope and built retaining walls from locally quarried bluestone, creating terraces that allowed him to work with the terrain. He later built another cabin around a large tree, which became his living quarters and was eventually known as the Inner Sanctum. From there, the project expanded through successive additions rather than according to a fixed architectural plan. Schmidt added rooms, corridors, elevated sections and other structures, connecting them with stairs, galleries, wooden walkways and balconies. The House of Mirrors developed as an interconnected environment that followed the contours of the mountainside rather than the conventions of a traditional house.The landscape continued to shape Schmidtâs approach. Instead of flattening the site to create a conventional building plot, he worked around the existing contours, fitting new sections around structures that were already in place. Walls followed the terrain and terraces stepped across the hillside, while each addition became part of a larger, increasingly complex environment. According to Ricco/Maresca, the House of Mirrors evolved organically as Schmidt continually added and altered elements in response to the landscape. Its windows and reflective surfaces became distinctive features, while the growing structure incorporated roughly 35 alcoves and caverns connected by corridors, galleries and staircases.Where discarded objects became part of the architectureSchmidtâs materials were as unconventional as his approach to construction. Alongside wood and stone, he incorporated mirrors, pieces of glass and objects that had little connection to traditional house building. Discarded items collected from around the area were given new roles within the structure, becoming part of its walls, surfaces and decorative elements. Woodstock Arts notes that Schmidt incorporated a striking assortment of found objects into the House of Mirrors, including car bumpers, wheels, bicycles, lawnmowers, guitars, saw blades, beer cans and doll parts.The result was an immersive environment in which ordinary building materials existed alongside reflections and found objects. Visitors could move through wooden passages and interconnected spaces containing glass, plants and handmade decorations. Some areas resembled grottoes, shrines or outdoor enclosures rather than conventional rooms. This approach placed Schmidt within the tradition of self-taught artists who created what are now known as art environments, works that blurred the boundaries between sculpture, architecture, gardening and everyday life. Rather than simply decorating a house, Schmidt transformed the structure itself into an evolving artwork.A fragile masterpiece that disappearedAs the structure became more elaborate, it also became increasingly fragile. Schmidt relied on improvised construction techniques and unconventional materials, including roofing tar, which he used to attach objects and coverings to parts of the structure. In January 1968, the House of Mirrors was destroyed by fire, leaving photographs and written accounts as the main records of the environment he had created. However, Schmidt continued building after the loss. He began another structure, known as Mark II, but it too was destroyed by fire in 1971. His work nevertheless left a lasting impression on other artists, including Philadelphia artist Isaiah Zagar. As a student at Pratt Institute, Zagar visited Woodstock and encountered Schmidtâs environment, an experience that influenced his ideas about art and later informed the development of Philadelphiaâs Magic Gardens.Schmidt died in 1978, while the House of Mirrors had already disappeared from the mountainside. Its legacy endured as an important example of an art environment created outside conventional architectural and artistic systems. Its significance lay not only in its extraordinary appearance, but also in the way Schmidt transformed an ordinary cabin into an evolving handmade world. He used materials around him, worked with the landscape and continued adding to the structure until architecture, sculpture and the mountainside became closely intertwined.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 47-year-old California pastor makes college football roster 30 years after an injury ended his career, inspired by a video of a 60-year-old player
articles.summary: US News: A 47-year-old California pastor has returned to college football nearly three decades after an injury ended his playing career, after his son showed h.
articles.body: A 47-year-old California pastor has returned to college football nearly three decades after an injury ended his playing career, after his son showed him a video of a 60-year-old man playing the sport. Justin Buzzard, a pastor, husband and father of three, has made the San JosÃ© City College Jaguars roster as a defensive end after spending years away from competitive football. Buzzard played football in high school and continued into college before injuries forced him to stop in the 1990s. Decades later, a video showing an older man playing football prompted his son to ask whether his father could make a similar comeback. Buzzard took the challenge seriously, began training again and eventually contacted San JosÃ© City College. After working through practices and conditioning with players far younger than him, he earned a place on the roster and is now preparing for the 2026 season.How a 47-year-old California pastor returned to college footballBuzzard's return began with a challenge from his son rather than a long-planned attempt to revive his football career. According to Buzzard's account to NBC Bay Area, his son showed him a social-media video featuring a man in his 60s playing football and questioned why his father could not get back on the field. Buzzard initially thought the suggestion was unrealistic, but the idea stayed with him. He eventually contacted San JosÃ© City College and asked about the possibility of joining the football programme. That conversation led to an opportunity to train with the team, where Buzzard had to demonstrate that he could handle the physical demands of college football. He began conditioning and participating in practices during the summer, working towards the same goal as much younger players. The decision represented a return to a sport he had left behind almost 30 years earlier after injuries ended his original playing career.An injury ended his first football career in the 1990sBuzzard already had years of football experience before his unusual comeback. He played four years of high-school football and then spent one year playing at college level, but injuries eventually forced him away from the sport. Nearly three decades later, he has returned to the field as a defensive end for the San JosÃ© City College Jaguars. His age makes the comeback unusual, but his previous experience also means he is not learning football from scratch. The challenge has instead been rebuilding the physical conditioning required to play a demanding contact sport after years away. Buzzard has spoken about wanting to remain healthy while competing alongside players who are young enough to be his children. His return is therefore not simply a symbolic appearance. He has gone through the process of training, practising and earning a place on the roster.He made the roster alongside much younger playersBuzzard's teammates are predominantly traditional college-age athletes, creating an enormous age gap between him and many of the people sharing the field. Reports say some of his teammates are around the age of his oldest son, yet Buzzard has said the players have welcomed him rather than treating him as an outsider. His teammates have reportedly given him the nickname "OG", reflecting his status as the oldest player in the group. San JosÃ© City College coach Jim Winkler told ChurchLeaders that Buzzard was expected to follow the same standards and rules as everyone else on the team. Buzzard has also made clear that he does not want younger players to go easy on him because of his age. His goal is to compete on the field rather than simply serve as an inspirational presence on the sidelines. The fact that he earned a roster place after going through the team's preparation process makes the comeback more significant than simply showing up for a practice.His family had concerns about the physical risksBuzzard's decision to return to contact football also required support from his family. He has been married for more than two decades and has three sons, and his wife initially had reservations about him actually playing in games. Buzzard told Fox News that she was happy for him to make the team but did not initially want him to take part in games because of the potential for injury. Her position later softened, and reports say she now has his games on her calendar and plans to support him. Buzzard has also emphasised the importance of staying healthy as he prepares for the season. The concern is understandable given that injuries were what ended his original football career. His comeback therefore involves a genuine physical risk, particularly because he is returning to a contact sport after a prolonged absence. Nevertheless, Buzzard has continued with the programme and has made clear that he wants to see how far he can take the opportunity.Football is now part of his life alongside his ministryBuzzard's return to the field is taking place alongside his work as a pastor. He is the founder and lead pastor of Garden City Church in the South Bay and has spent years speaking about personal growth, fatherhood, relationships and taking meaningful risks. His football comeback has naturally become connected to that message. Buzzard has described his philosophy with the phrase "risk or rust", arguing that people should continue challenging themselves rather than allowing fear or comfort to prevent them from pursuing meaningful goals. The football experiment gives him a personal example of that philosophy. He is attempting something physically demanding that he had not done for decades while continuing his responsibilities as a pastor, husband and father. His return has therefore become more than a sports story for him. It is also an example of the idea that people can revisit ambitions they once considered finished.His goal is to compete during the 2026 seasonMaking the roster was only the first milestone in Buzzard's comeback. He wants to remain healthy, participate in the season and have an opportunity to contribute on the field. He wears No. 48, a reference to the age he will turn in September. His preparation has involved training alongside much younger athletes, and he has said that he does not expect special treatment because of his age. The San JosÃ© City College Jaguars are preparing for the 2026 season, giving Buzzard the opportunity to turn an unusual comeback story into an actual competitive season. How much playing time he receives remains to be seen, and simply making the roster does not guarantee that he will appear regularly in games. For now, however, he has achieved the part that once seemed almost impossible. A career that ended with injury in the 1990s has been revived nearly three decades later, after a conversation with his son gave him the push to try again.A decades-old football dream has a second chanceBuzzard's story stands out because the comeback was not the result of a professional opportunity or a carefully planned athletic campaign. It began with his son showing him a video of an older football player and asking a simple question. Buzzard could have dismissed the idea because of his age, his previous injuries or the decades that had passed since he last played. Instead, he decided to find out whether a return was possible. He trained, approached a college programme and eventually earned his place alongside players decades younger than him. Whether he becomes a regular contributor during the season remains uncertain, but the achievement has already given him the chance to finish a chapter that was abruptly ended by injury. For Buzzard, the return to football is also an opportunity to demonstrate the message he has encouraged others to follow: an old setback does not necessarily have to determine what comes next.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1917, the Crane family bought the first piece of Choate Island; decades later, the island entered the Crane Wildlife Refuge under the Trustees in 1974
articles.summary: US News: Explore the fascinating transformation of Choate Island from a thriving agricultural landscape to a protected wildlife refuge. Discover its historical significance, diverse ecosystems, and the legacy of the Crane family.
articles.body: For centuries, the island supported Indigenous communities, farms, livestock and family homes before becoming a wildlife refuge on the Massachusetts coast. Choate Island, once known as Hog Island, is now the largest island in the Crane Wildlife Refuge, where salt marsh, grassland and forest frame historic buildings that date back more than two centuries. Its transformation was gradual, beginning with the Crane family's early-20th-century land purchases and ending with MinÃ© Crane's 1974 gift to The Trustees of Reservations.According to The Trustees of Reservations, Choate Island is the largest island in the Crane Wildlife Refuge, covering 135 acres within the refugeâs 697-acre network of coastal islands and marshes in the Essex River Estuary. More than 200 bird species have been recorded across the refuge, while Choate Island provides habitat for mammals including deer, fisher, coyotes and otters. Its spruce forest supports birds such as golden-crowned kinglets and sharp-shinned hawks, while its grasslands provide important habitat for bobolinks and Savannah sparrows.From Indigenous land to a farming islandAccording to Babson Historical Society, Indigenous communities in the region had established agricultural settlements and maintained a mixed subsistence economy based on farming, fishing, hunting and shellfish gathering. The Agawam and other Indigenous communities used the coastal landscape and surrounding estuaries long before the Crane family arrived, while the islands later became part of a farming landscape that remained important through the 18th and 19th centuries.European settlers later called Choate Island âHog Islandâ, reflecting its role in the regionâs colonial farming system. The Choate family became closely associated with the island after Thomas Choate acquired land there in the late 17th century, with subsequent generations developing and maintaining farms for generations. The Choate House, built in the early to mid-18th century, became the centre of the familyâs long presence. Choate Island and neighbouring Long Island were connected by a causeway, allowing people, livestock and agricultural goods to move between them, while fields, grazing areas, stone walls and farm buildings developed alongside salt marshes and tidal waters. The island was officially renamed Choate Island in 1887.The Cranes arriveThe Trustees of Reservations also note that the next major change came in the early 20th century, when Richard T. Crane Jr., the Chicago industrialist who was developing the Crane Estate around Castle Hill, acquired the first portion of Choate Island in 1917. The Crane family expanded its holdings in 1927, bringing more of the island into the estate. Rather than removing every trace of its agricultural past, the Cranes retained historic structures, including the Choate House and the nearby Proctor Barn on Long Island, while reshaping parts of the landscape for their own use.One of the most visible changes was tree planting, with Cornelius Crane establishing about 95 acres of spruce and pine forest on Choate Island in the 1930s. Norway spruce became one of the dominant species, creating a prominent new feature in the islandâs landscape. Over the decades, however, severe storms damaged large sections of the ageing plantation, prompting The Trustees to remove about 30 acres of trees and restore the area as shrubland and young forest habitat. Crane and his wife, MinÃ©, also developed a strong personal connection with the island, using the White Cottage, designed by architect Royal Barry Wills, as a private retreat overlooking Ipswich Bay and the surrounding marshes. The couple were later buried near the islandâs summit, where their graves overlook the landscape that had become an important part of their lives.From private estate to wildlife refugeAccording to Historic Massachusetts, MinÃ© Crane donated about 700 acres of land, including Choate Island and surrounding islands and salt marshes, to The Trustees of Reservations in 1974 in memory of her husband, Cornelius Crane. The gift formed the foundation of the Crane Wildlife Refuge, which was later expanded through additional acquisitions and donations. The transition from private estate to protected refuge did not mean freezing the landscape in its historic state. Instead, conservation work has continued to respond to changing ecological conditions. In 2017, for example, The Trustees and conservation partners cleared about 30 acres of ageing Norway spruce plantation after severe storms had damaged large sections of the forest. The project created space for shrubland and young forest habitat, supporting species including American black ducks, American woodcocks, eastern towhees and native pollinators. This approach reflects a broader conservation goal: maintaining a functioning coastal ecosystem rather than preserving every element of the landscape exactly as the Cranes left it. Today, visitors can follow gravel roads and mown trails past the historic Choate House towards the Crane burial site near the islandâs highest point. The route passes through a changing landscape of grassland, woodland, shoreline and salt marsh, showing how natural habitats and historic features coexist on the island.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: How a family reunion in China ended in a 3-year prison term for artist Gao Zhen
articles.summary: China News: A family visit to China back in August 2024 ended with a three-year prison sentence for a US-based Chinese artist. Gao Zhen, a member of the artistic .
articles.body: A family visit to China back in August 2024 ended with a three-year prison sentence for a US-based Chinese artist. Gao Zhen, a member of the artistic duo the Gao brothers, was given the prison sentence over a satirical artwork involving statues of Mao Zedong.Gao was sentenced on Tuesday by the Sanhei People's Court in northern Hebei province for âinfringing upon the reputation of heroesâ, according to his wife, Zhao Yaliang. The offence relates to artworks that Chinese authorities consider insulting to revolutionary figures.The sentence brought an abrupt end to hopes that Gao, who has remained in official custody since his arrest, would soon be released and return to his family in the US. Zhao said she had prepared clothes for her husband, expecting that he might be freed.âI felt two years was my limit, and I was really disappointed and sad. I haven't been able to catch my breath,â she said.Gao was arrested while visiting family in China in August 2024, after travelling back from the US, where he and his family had immigrated. He has remained in custody for about two years since then.The case centres on several of Gao's satirical works, including Maoâs Guilt, a 2009 statue depicting Mao Zedong, the founder of modern China, kneeling in repentance. Another is the Miss Mao series, which caricatures Mao with breasts and an exaggerated nose.Gao's supporters say the works predate the law under which he was prosecuted. Shane Yi, a researcher at Chinese Human Rights Defenders who has advocated for the artist, said Gao plans to appeal.Yi described the case as âa very clear case of a violation of a personâs freedom of expression.âThe court did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Amnesty International also criticised the conviction, saying the sentence was intended to discourage artists from challenging official narratives. Gao was handed the maximum three-year prison term available under the offence.âThe lengthy pre-trial detention and, ultimately, decision to convict Gao Zhen and sentence him to the maximum three-year prison term under this offence illustrate the authoritiesâ determination to deter others from engaging in independent artistic expression,â said Amnesty's China Director Sarah Brooks.âNo artist should face criminal punishment for creating work that challenges official narratives or encourages critical reflection on history,â she said.The Gao Brothers became internationally known for works examining authoritarianism and censorship. Their art was exhibited in China and abroad during a period of relative openness in the country.That space for political expression has narrowed in recent years, particularly when artists and others have addressed prominent political figures. China passed a law in 2018 banning criticism of the nation's âheroesâ, which authorities have since used in cases involving depictions of revolutionary figures.For Zhao, however, the case remains deeply personal. She said she hopes to be reunited with her husband and return with him to the US. Chinese courts often count time spent in pre-trial detention as time served towards a prison sentence.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
